title: Finite adjoin with fraction field and integral-closure map
statement: For a domain B and its fraction field K, the subalgebra generated by two elements of integralClosure B K is finite over B, has fraction field K, and admits the compatible injective map into the integral closure with surjective map on prime spectra.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2, adjoin and lying-over paragraphs

proof.text: Let A be Algebra.adjoin B {x, y}. The generators belong to integralClosure B K, so Algebra.adjoin_le gives A ≤ integralClosure B K. Apply Algebra.finite_adjoin_of_finite_of_isIntegral to the finite two-element set. The instance Localization.subalgebra.instIsFractionRingSubtypeMemSubalgebra gives IsFractionRing A K for any subalgebra of the fraction field. Algebra.subset_adjoin places x and y in A.

Define g as the ring homomorphism underlying Subalgebra.inclusion of A into integralClosure B K. Subalgebra.inclusion_injective proves injectivity; the equality of the underlying K-elements and compatibility with the B-algebra maps are reflexive. The composite of g with algebraMap B A equals algebraMap B (integralClosure B K). The latter is integral by the integral-closure instance; RingHom.IsIntegral.tower_top makes g integral. Apply RingHom.IsIntegral.comap_surjective to g and its injectivity.

proof_origin.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2, adjoin and lying-over paragraphs; formalized directly using Mathlib by D3

lean.statement:
theorem exists_adjoin_finite_fraction_spec
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra B K] [IsFractionRing B K]
    (x y : integralClosure B K) :
    ∃ A : Subalgebra B K, Module.Finite B A ∧ IsFractionRing A K ∧
      (x : K) ∈ A ∧ (y : K) ∈ A ∧
      ∃ g : A →+* (integralClosure B K), Function.Injective g ∧
        (∀ z : A, (g z : K) = z) ∧
        (∀ b : B, g (algebraMap B A b) = algebraMap B (integralClosure B K) b) ∧
        Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap g)
